chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Hammam ibn Uthman from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in

A man divorced his wife, then left her until her waiting period expired, then he married her, then he divorced her without having intercourse with her, then he married her again, then he divorced her before having intercourse with her, until he did that to her three times. He said: She is not permissible to him until she marries a husband other than him.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man divorces his wife three times without having intercourse with her?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies the Shia juristic view that three divorces without consummation (dakhil) still trigger the 'Tanzil' rule, requiring a subsequent marriage to a third party before the first husband can remarry her. Unlike the Hanafi school which often treats these as three distinct divorces, Shia scholarship emphasizes the continuity of the marital bond until actual consummation, making the third 'divorce' a formal severance. This ruling underscores the importance of 'Nikah al-Mu'akkadah' (solemnized marriage) with the third party to restore permissibility.
